'''RBC Capital Markets''' is a global [[investment bank]] providing services in banking, finance, and [[capital market]]s to corporations, [[institutional investor]]s, asset managers, and governments globally. Locations span 55 offices in 16 countries across North America, the UK, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region. Employment estimates for RBC professionals are roughly 7,600 per company reports.<ref name="our-offices">{{Cite web |url=https://www.rbccm.com/en/offices/our-offices |title=Our Offices {{!}} RBC Capital Markets |url-status=live |website=RBC Capital Markets |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities Inc. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516154923/https://www.rbccm.com/en/our-offices |archive-date=2026-05-16}}</ref> Services provided include insights required to raise capital, access markets, mitigate risk, and acquire or dispose of assets for clients worldwide.

==Overview==
RBC Capital Markets is part of [[Royal Bank of Canada]] (RBC). Operating since 1864, RBC is the seventh largest in North America and the 11th largest bank globally as measured by market capitalization.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://business.financialpost.com/news/fp-street/rbc-cracks-wall-streets-top-10-list-for-advising-on-ma-deals |title=Royal Bank of Canada cracks Wall Street's top 10 list for advising on M&A deals |newspaper=Financial Post |date=22 October 2019 |access-date=April 9, 2020|last1=Alexander |first1=Doug }}</ref> Royal Bank of Canada maintains its position as the safest bank in North America. Canadian banks dominate the list once again, taking the top seven spots.<ref>[https://gfmag.com/award/winner-announcements/press-release-global-finance-names-the-safest-banks-in-north-america-2025/ PRESS RELEASE: Global Finance Names The Safest Banks In North America 2025]</ref>

== History ==

RBC Capital Markets traces its origins to 1864, when the Merchants' Bank was founded in Halifax, Nova Scotia, by a group of eight maritime merchants.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating 150 years: A look back at where RBC came from |url=https://www.rbcwealthmanagement.com/en-ca/community/insights/celebrating-150-years-a-look-back-at-where-rbc-came-from |publisher=RBC Wealth Management |date=November 26, 2018 |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> Over more than 160 years, the institution evolved through a series of renamings, strategic acquisitions, and global expansions to become one of the leading investment banks in North America.<ref>{{cite web |title=History |url=https://www.rbccm.com/en/about-us/history.page |publisher=RBC Capital Markets |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

=== The Beginning (Pre-1901) ===

In 1864, eight prominent Halifax business figures — including Thomas C. Kinnear, Edward Kenny, and William Cunard — established the Merchants' Bank on the Halifax waterfront to provide credit to merchants importing and exporting through the port.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating 150 years: A look back at where RBC came from |url=https://www.rbcwealthmanagement.com/en-ca/community/insights/celebrating-150-years-a-look-back-at-where-rbc-came-from |publisher=RBC Wealth Management |date=November 26, 2018 |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> The bank began with approximately $200,000 in capital and grew alongside the surge in commercial activity driven by the American Civil War, during which Halifax served as a hub for cross-border trade.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Royal Bank of Canada — History |url=http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/the-royal-bank-of-canada-history/ |publisher=FundingUniverse |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

On June 22, 1869 — shortly after Canadian Confederation — the institution received a federal charter and was formally incorporated as the '''Merchants' Bank of Halifax'''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Virtual Exhibits |url=https://www.rbc.com/en/about-us/history/virtual-exhibits/ |publisher=Royal Bank of Canada |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> The first corporate seal adopted at incorporation depicted a three-mast sailing ship, reportedly belonging to founding director William Cunard, reflecting the institution's maritime identity.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating Our History |url=https://www.rbc.com/en/about-us/history/celebrating-our-history/ |publisher=Royal Bank of Canada |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> Thomas C. Kinnear served as its first president.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Royal Bank of Canada — History |url=http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/the-royal-bank-of-canada-history/ |publisher=FundingUniverse |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

By 1893, the Merchants' Bank of Halifax became a publicly traded company, listing on the Montreal Exchange.<ref>{{cite web |title=Royal Bank of Canada |url=https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/business-and-management/royal-bank-canada |publisher=EBSCO Research Starters |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> In its early decades, the bank maintained a strong presence throughout the Maritimes while forging correspondent banking relationships in New York and London.<ref>{{cite web |title=Royal Bank of Canada |url=https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/business-and-management/royal-bank-canada |publisher=EBSCO Research Starters |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

=== Going National (1901–1962) ===

In 1901, following a boardroom victory by executives who supported westward expansion, the institution was renamed '''The Royal Bank of Canada'''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating 150 years: A look back at where RBC came from |url=https://www.rbcwealthmanagement.com/en-ca/community/insights/celebrating-150-years-a-look-back-at-where-rbc-came-from |publisher=RBC Wealth Management |date=November 26, 2018 |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> The name change reflected the bank's national ambitions; by this time, branches were operating coast to coast, with several opened in British Columbia to serve the Klondike Gold Rush.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating 150 years: A look back at where RBC came from |url=https://www.rbcwealthmanagement.com/en-ca/community/insights/celebrating-150-years-a-look-back-at-where-rbc-came-from |publisher=RBC Wealth Management |date=November 26, 2018 |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> At the time of the renaming, the bank operated 64 branches across the country.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Royal Bank of Canada |url=https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/royal-bank-of-canada |encyclopedia=The Canadian Encyclopedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

To accompany the new name, a revised corporate seal was commissioned featuring a heraldic design — a unicorn, a lion, a quartered shield, and the royal motto ''Dieu et Mon Droit'' — which became the Royal Bank's first publicly recognized symbol both domestically and internationally.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating Our History |url=https://www.rbc.com/en/about-us/history/celebrating-our-history/ |publisher=Royal Bank of Canada |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> In 1903, the bank opened its first Toronto branch. In 1907, the board approved moving the head office from Halifax to Montreal.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Royal Bank of Canada |url=https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/royal-bank-of-canada |encyclopedia=The Canadian Encyclopedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> By 1908, branches had been established in every provincial capital under the presidency of Herbert Holt, a prominent Montreal businessman.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Royal Bank of Canada |url=https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/royal-bank-of-canada |encyclopedia=The Canadian Encyclopedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

During this same period, in 1901, a separate firm — '''Dominion Securities Corporation Limited''' — was incorporated in Toronto.<ref>{{cite web |title=A proud history |url=https://ca.rbcwealthmanagement.com/documents/507229/3835907/RBC+DS+-+A+proud+history.pdf |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> Founded independently of the Royal Bank, Dominion Securities initially focused on government and municipal bonds, and would later become a foundational institution in the development of the Canadian bond market.<ref>{{cite web |title=History |url=https://www.rbccm.com/en/about-us/history.page |publisher=RBC Capital Markets |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> Its business expanded significantly during the First World War through the issuance of war bonds.<ref>{{cite web |title=A proud history |url=https://ca.rbcwealthmanagement.com/documents/507229/3835907/RBC+DS+-+A+proud+history.pdf |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

=== An Iconic Emblem (1962–2001) ===

In 1962, the Royal Bank of Canada introduced its first purpose-built corporate logo: a heraldic emblem incorporating a lion symbolizing strength, a crown representing royal heritage, and a globe signifying global presence.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating Our History |url=https://www.rbc.com/en/about-us/history/celebrating-our-history/ |publisher=Royal Bank of Canada |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> The logo quickly became one of the most recognizable corporate symbols in Canada and remained in use for nearly four decades.

Meanwhile, Dominion Securities continued to grow as Canada's leading independent investment dealer. In 1937, a stock trading department was added, completing the firm's full-service investment capabilities.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Brief Timeline of Our History |url=http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities (archived) |access-date=June 10, 2026 |archive-date=May 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516075607/http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1984, Dominion Securities expanded through the acquisition of Pitfield, Mackay, Ross Limited.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Brief Timeline of Our History |url=http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities (archived) |access-date=June 10, 2026 |archive-date=May 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516075607/http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The regulatory environment shifted decisively in 1987, when the deregulation of Canadian securities law — colloquially known as the "Little Bang" — permitted Canadian banks to enter the securities business for the first time.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=RBC Dominion Securities |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RBC_Dominion_Securities |encyclopedia=Wikipedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> On March 31, 1988, the Royal Bank of Canada acquired a 67 per cent stake in Dominion Securities Inc. for $385 million, subsequently renaming the firm '''RBC Dominion Securities Inc.'''<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=RBC Dominion Securities |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RBC_Dominion_Securities |encyclopedia=Wikipedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> In 1989, RBC Dominion Securities further grew through the acquisition of Pemberton Willoughby Investment Corporation.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Brief Timeline of Our History |url=http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities (archived) |access-date=June 10, 2026 |archive-date=May 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516075607/http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 1995, the New York office of RBC Dominion Securities acquired Kidder Peabody's equity derivatives group, leading to the formation of the Global Equity Derivatives (GED) group — an early step toward combining the bank's corporate banking strength with new investment banking capabilities.<ref>{{cite web |title=Our Business in the U.S. |url=https://www.rbc.com/en/about-us/history/milestones-at-a-glance/our-business-in-the-u-s/ |publisher=Royal Bank of Canada |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> In 1996, the Royal Bank acquired full, 100 per cent ownership of Dominion Securities Inc., and that same year RBC Dominion Securities acquired Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd. for $480 million.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Royal Bank of Canada |url=https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/royal-bank-of-canada |encyclopedia=The Canadian Encyclopedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Brief Timeline of Our History |url=http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities (archived) |access-date=June 10, 2026 |archive-date=May 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516075607/http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Looking Forward (2001–Present) ===

In 2000, the investment banking operations of RBC Dominion Securities were rebranded as '''RBC Capital Markets''', marking the formal establishment of a dedicated global capital markets platform.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=RBC Dominion Securities |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RBC_Dominion_Securities |encyclopedia=Wikipedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> The following year, RBC Capital Markets expanded its North American presence significantly through the acquisition of U.S.-based investment firm [[Dain Rauscher Wessels]] for approximately US$1.46 billion, and the subsequent integration of Tucker Anthony Sutro & Co.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=Royal Bank of Canada |url=https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/royal-bank-of-canada |encyclopedia=The Canadian Encyclopedia |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Brief Timeline of Our History |url=http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |publisher=RBC Dominion Securities (archived) |access-date=June 10, 2026 |archive-date=May 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516075607/http://www.rbcds.com/dominion-securities-history.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Concurrent with this expansion, in 2001 the Royal Bank of Canada launched a new corporate master brand — the modern '''RBC''' logo — characterized by a simplified lion-and-globe design set against a blue background.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating Our History |url=https://www.rbc.com/en/about-us/history/celebrating-our-history/ |publisher=Royal Bank of Canada |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> The redesign reflected the organization's evolution into a diversified global financial services company while retaining visual continuity with the heraldic tradition established in 1962.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrating Our History |url=https://www.rbc.com/en/about-us/history/celebrating-our-history/ |publisher=Royal Bank of Canada |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>

Today, RBC Capital Markets operates as the investment banking and capital markets division of [[Royal Bank of Canada]], employing roughly 7,600 professionals across 55 offices in 16 countries throughout North America, the United Kingdom, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region.<ref name="our-offices"/> The firm provides services in equity and debt underwriting, mergers and acquisitions, sales and trading, and financial advisory to corporations, institutional investors, asset managers, private equity firms, and governments worldwide.<ref>{{cite web |title=History |url=https://www.rbccm.com/en/about-us/history.page |publisher=RBC Capital Markets |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref>
